meta.title: Ch 16: Professional and Ethical Duty of a Chartered Accountant — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 16 (Professional and Ethical Duty of a Chartered Accountant).

questions.q: A CA firm's fees from a non-listed audit client for a year are Rs 90 lakh, of which Rs 60 lakh are for book-keeping. Under the ICAI Code of Ethics, this primarily creates a:
o: Self-review threat, in addition to a management-participation issue the Code prohibits for the same financial statements
questions.why: Preparing the books and then auditing them = self-review threat; assuming management functions is prohibited (self-review/management-participation). Advocacy is promoting a client's position; intimidation is coercion — neither fits.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — threat-classification questions dominate the ethics MCQs Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Threat five-pack: Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, Intimidation — match the FACTS, not the feeling.

questions.q: A member in practice invites a prospective client's purchase manager for lunch to obtain an audit assignment. Under the Code of Ethics, solicitation of clients by a member in practice is:
o: Prohibited — members shall not solicit work by personal communication/corruption, inducement etc.
A fundamental-principle breach only for listed audits
questions.why: Part III of the First Schedule (Sections 251–267 of the Code) bars soliciting clients personally/by agents; inducements like hospitality to win work fall within the prohibition. ICAI ethics rules are stricter than the generic threats framework here.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the solicitation bar is a guaranteed objective-question zone AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: No chasing clients: personal canvassing, agents, and inducements are barred for members in practice. Clients should come to you, not the lunch to them.

questions.q: Under the ICAI Code, when no specific provision addresses a situation, a member should:
o: Identify threats, evaluate significance, and apply safeguards; withdraw if threats cannot be reduced
questions.why: The conceptual framework approach applies fundamental principles: identify → evaluate threats → apply safeguards; if safeguards are unavailable/insufficient, decline or continue only per Code hierarchy.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the framework approach is the preamble every attempt tests Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: No rule? No problem: identify, evaluate, safeguard, withdraw. The framework is the backstop for every gap.

questions.q: Disclosure of client information without specific permission is permitted under the Code:
o: Whenever the audit team deems it useful
Where there is a legal or professional duty to disclose (e.g., court order) or permitted by law
For the successor auditor, without inquiry
questions.why: The Code permits/obliges disclosure for professional/legal duty (e.g., reporting under statute, responding to inquiries with permissions); the successor-auditor inquiry has its own protocol requiring client consent.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — confidentiality carve-outs are frequent 1-markers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Confidentiality's three doors: duty (legal), permission (client), quality/professional review — knock with a written reason.

questions.q: For listed-entity audits, the ICAI/Code provisions on key audit partner rotation generally require cooling-off periods aimed at:
o: Reducing familiarity and self-interest threats from long association
questions.why: Partner rotation/cooling-off addresses familiarity/self-interest threats from long tenure of the same personnel on an engagement team.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — rotation and cooling-off as safeguard types are pattern-tested AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Long familiarity softens scepticism; rotation re-hardens it — the safeguard attacks the threat type, not the person.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five fundamental principles of the ICAI Code of Ethics?
questions.why: Five principles: Integrity; Objectivity; Professional competence & due care; Confidentiality; Professional behaviour. Prudence is an accounting/auditing idea, not a Code principle.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the five-list 'except' format is the ethics freebie AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Five pillars: Integrity, Objectivity, Competence, Confidentiality, Conduct. Prudence lives in accounts, not ethics.

questions.q: For a non-assurance engagement for an audit client, threats to independence are evaluated with reference to:
o: Whether the NAES results in management decisions being made and the nature/scope of the audit — safeguards or decline
questions.why: The Code requires evaluating whether NAES affects independence (self-review if it influences accounting records/FS or management decisions); safeguards may reduce, else decline/withdraw the NAES (or audit as last resort per hierarchy).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — hierarchy-of-response logic is tested with twists Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: If the bookkeeping contaminates the audit lens, no fee can buy independence — shed the NAES before the audit.

questions.q: A contingent fee arrangement for professional services is permitted under the ICAI Code:
o: For tax return preparation for the client always
Generally restricted — fees determined by the result of the transaction create self-interest threats (esp. for audit/assurance)
When the client is a government entity
questions.why: Contingent fees for assurance/audit-like services create self-interest threats and are barred/limited (with narrow permitted situations e.g. certain tax proceedings outcomes under Code carve-outs); never for auditing FS.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — fee-structure threat identification Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Fee rides on the outcome, judgment wobbles — assurance work stays off the rollercoaster.

questions.q: Marketing that discredits a rival practitioner breaches:
o: Professional behaviour (and Code bars adverse publicity)
questions.why: The Code prohibits solicitation/adverse publicity; professional behaviour requires compliance with laws and avoiding disrepute.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — which-principle-matches-which-fact Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Trash another firm = professional-behaviour breach; the principle list is matched by fact-type, not by feeling.

questions.topic: Code — conflict of interest for NAES
questions.q: Accepting a non-audit engagement where a conflict with another client's interest arises, the member must:
o: Disclose the conflict to both clients and proceed with informed consent or decline
questions.why: Conflicts-of-interest provisions require disclosure to affected clients and informed consent, or decline/withdraw — confidentiality is respected in the disclosure (no details).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — disclose-and-consent mechanics AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Code — conflict of interest for NAES
mem.tip: When two clients pull, let them both see the rope — then decide.

questions.why: SA 230: assemble the final file promptly (usually ≤60 days) and retain ≥5 years (or per law). Note the difference: ICAI Code/SA retention vs SEBI 8-year records for listed-auditors in some contexts.

questions.q: A CA in practice may accept an audit assignment with unpaid fees of the predecessor auditor:
o: With the predecessor's consent/after ensuring no professional bar exists (communication with incumbent is mandatory before accepting)
questions.why: Sec 259/Code: professional communication with the incumbent before accepting the offer is mandatory; unpaid-fees situations require attention under the Code's rules on transferring engagements.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the etiquette rule tested as law Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Say hello (and check why the last man left) before you sign.
